title: Texas's 2nd Congressional District Election, 2026
description: An open-seat race for Texas's 2nd Congressional District after Republican state Representative Steve Toth defeated four-term incumbent Dan Crenshaw in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary. The district covers parts of Harris and Montgomery Counties north of Houston, including The Woodlands, Humble, and Atascocita. Toth, a conservative firebrand and Texas House member, faces Democrat Shaun Finnie, a first-time candidate and investment banker who promotes fiscal moderation and protecting entitlement programs. The Cook Political Report rates the district as Solid Republican, giving Toth a strong advantage in the general election.
polling_note: No district-specific general election polls were found for Texas's 2nd Congressional District as of June 2026.

candidates.name: Shaun Finnie
candidates.summary: Shaun Finnie is a senior advisor at Evercore and a first-time candidate running for U.S. House in Texas's 2nd Congressional District. He promotes fiscal responsibility, protecting Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid, eliminating tariffs, and investing in public education and medical research. Finnie holds a law degree from the University of Western Ontario and an MBA from Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management, and previously practiced oil and gas law before a career in investment banking.

candidates.name: Steve Toth
candidates.summary: Steve Toth is a Texas state representative and businessman who defeated four-term incumbent Dan Crenshaw in the March 2026 Republican primary for Texas's 2nd Congressional District. He is a conservative firebrand who has served in the Texas House from District 15 (The Woodlands area) since 2019, and previously served from 2013 to 2015. Toth owns pool companies, is a former pastor, and has authored legislation on Second Amendment protections, abortion restrictions, and government transparency.
